sentences.text: Kazaklambia is morphologically distinct from other Eurasian taxa and juveniles of similar age due to a thickened dome on the postorbital bone, doming of the nasal bone, and a frontal length-to-width ratio of less than one.
The animal is known from the juvenile holotype specimen PIN 2230, which lacks the snout, lower jaw front, some dorsal vertebrae, and the tail tip.
The species name 'convincens' refers to the specimen being the most complete dinosaur ever found in the Soviet Union at the time, proving dinosaurs existed in that geological horizon.
This nearly complete skeleton is missing only the snout, hands, left foot, and tail tip, making it the most complete dinosaur known from the former Soviet Union.
A nearly complete hadrosaurid skeleton was discovered in 1961 at the Syuk-Syuk locality in southern Kazakhstan, 45 km north of Tashkent.
Soviet paleontologist Anatoly Konstantinovich Rozhdestvensky described the species as Procheneosaurus convincens in 1968.
Canadian paleontologists Phil R. Bell and Kirstin S. Brink revisited and partly redescribed the taxon in 2013, focusing on the skull.
Bell and Brink assigned Kazaklambia to the Lambeosaurinae subfamily in a basal position in 2013.
A 2021 phylogenetic analysis identified Kazaklambia as a primitive member of the Lambeosaurini tribe, though broader relationships within Lambeosaurinae remain unresolved.
Kazaklambia convincens lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous Santonian stage, approximately between 86.3 and 83.6 million years ago.
American paleontologist Peter Dodson rejected Procheneosaurus as a distinct genus in 1975, creating uncertainty about the validity of P. convincens.
There is a debate regarding the species' validity, with some researchers considering it a synonym of Jaxartosaurus while others support its separation based on skull anatomy.
